title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 愍懷太子
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
units.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.
units.idiomatic: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.

units.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
units.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
units.idiomatic: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

units.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
units.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.
units.idiomatic: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.

title.zh: 卷三十九 雜傳第二十七: 王鎔 羅紹威 王處直 劉守光
title.en: Volume 39 Miscellaneous Biographies 19: Wang Rong, Luo Shaowei, Wang Chuzhi, Liu Shouguang
title.raw: 卷三十九 雜傳第二十七: 王鎔 羅紹威 王處直 劉守光 Volume 39 Miscellaneous Biographies 19: Wang Rong, Luo Shaowei, Wang Chuzhi, Liu Shouguang

units.zh: 王镕，其先回鶻阿布思之遺種，曰沒諾幹，為鎮州王武俊騎將，武俊錄以為子，遂冒姓王氏。
units.literal: Wang Rong: his ancestors were descendants of the Uyghur Abu Si, named Mo Nuogan, a cavalry officer of Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou; Wujun adopted him as a son, and he took the surname Wang.
units.idiomatic: Wang Rong traced his line to Mo Nuogan, a survivor of the Uyghur chief Abu Si. Mo Nuogan served Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou as a mounted officer; Wujun adopted him, and the family took the name Wang.

units.zh: 沒諾幹子曰末垣活，末垣活子曰升，升子曰廷湊，廷湊子曰元達，元達子曰紹鼎、紹懿，紹鼎子曰景崇。
units.literal: Mo Nuogan’s son was Mo Yuanhuo; Mo Yuanhuo’s son was Sheng; Sheng’s son was Tingcou; Tingcou’s son was Yuanda; Yuanda’s sons were Shaoding and Shaoyi; Shaoding’s son was Jingchong.
units.idiomatic: Mo Nuogan begat Mo Yuanhuo, who begat Sheng, then Tingcou, then Yuanda. Yuanda had Shaoding and Shaoyi; Shaoding begat Jingchong.

units.zh: 自升以上三世，常為鎮州騎將，自景崇以上四世五人，皆為成德軍節度使。
units.literal: From Sheng upward for three generations they were constantly Zhenzhou cavalry officers; from Jingchong upward for four generations five men all were military commissioners of the Chengde army.
units.idiomatic: For three generations before Sheng the family held cavalry commands at Zhenzhou; for four generations from Jingchong, five men in succession ruled Chengde.

units.zh: 景崇官至守太尉，封常山郡王，唐中和二年卒。
units.literal: Jingchong reached the office of Acting Grand Marshal, was enfeoffed Prince of Changshan, and died in the second year of Tang Zhonghe.
units.idiomatic: Jingchong rose to Acting Grand Marshal and Prince of Changshan; he died in Zhonghe 2 of Tang.

units.zh: 子鎔立，年十歲。
units.literal: His son Rong succeeded, ten years old.
units.idiomatic: His son Rong succeeded him at the age of ten.

units.zh: 是時，晉新有太原，李匡威據幽州，王處存據中山，赫連鐸據大同，孟方立據邢臺，四面豪傑並起而交爭。
units.literal: At that time Jin had newly taken Taiyuan; Li Kuangwei held Youzhou, Wang Chucun held Zhongshan, Helian Duo held Datong, and Meng Fangli held Xingtai—heroes rose on every side and fought one another.
units.idiomatic: Jin had just secured Taiyuan. Li Kuangwei held Youzhou, Wang Chucun Zhongshan, Helian Duo Datong, Meng Fangli Xingtai—warlords sprang up on all sides and tore at one another.

units.zh: 镕介於其間，而承祖父百年之業，士馬強而畜積富，為唐累世藩臣。
units.literal: Rong stood between them, yet inherited his grandfather’s enterprise of a hundred years: strong soldiers and horses, rich stores—a Tang frontier house for generations.
units.idiomatic: Rong sat in the middle of them all, heir to a century of Wang power: strong cavalry, deep granaries, a Tang vassal line for generations.

units.zh: 故镕年雖少，藉其世家以取重，四方諸鎮廢立承繼，有請於唐者，皆因镕以聞。
units.literal: Thus though Rong was young, he drew weight from his house; when the circuits sought Tang’s approval for deposition, succession, or appointment, the petition always went through Rong.
units.idiomatic: Young as he was, the Wang name gave him weight. Whenever a circuit asked the court to confirm a change of ruler, the word passed through Rong.

units.zh: 自晉兵出山東，已破孟遷，取邢、洺、磁三州，景福元年，乃大舉擊趙，下臨城。
units.literal: When Jin armies marched out from Shandong they had already broken Meng Qian and taken Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures. In Jingfu 1 they launched a major assault on Zhao and took Lincheng.
units.idiomatic: Once Jin marched out of Shandong it had already broken Meng Qian and taken Xing, Ming, and Ci. In Jingfu 1 it struck Zhao in force and took Lincheng.

units.zh: 鎔求救於李匡威，匡威來救，晉軍解去。
units.literal: Rong begged Li Kuangwei for rescue; Kuangwei came and Jin withdrew.
units.idiomatic: Rong called on Li Kuangwei; Kuangwei marched to save him and Jin pulled back.

units.zh: 明年，晉會王處存攻鎔堅固、新市。
units.literal: The next year Jin joined Wang Chucun to attack Jangu and Xinshi.
units.idiomatic: The next year Jin and Wang Chucun attacked Jangu and Xinshi.

units.zh: 晉王與處存皆自將，而鎔未嘗臨軍，遣追風都團練使段亮、翦寇都團練使馬珂等，以兵屬匡威而已。
units.literal: The Prince of Jin and Chucun both commanded in person, but Rong never went to the field himself—he sent Duan Liang, regimental training commissioner of Pursuing Wind, Ma Ke, regimental training commissioner of Shearing Bandits, and others, placing the troops under Kuangwei only.
units.idiomatic: Both commanders led in person, but Rong never took the field—he sent Duan Liang of Pursuing Wind and Ma Ke of Shearing Bandits and left the troops to Kuangwei.

units.zh: 匡威戰磁河，晉軍大敗。
units.literal: Kuangwei fought at Ci River and Jin was badly defeated.
units.idiomatic: At Ci River Kuangwei smashed the Jin army.

units.zh: 明年春，晉攻天長軍，鎔出兵救之，敗于叱日嶺，晉軍遂出井陘。
units.literal: The next spring Jin attacked Tianchang Garrison. Rong sent troops to relieve it, was beaten at Chiri Ridge, and Jin marched out through Jingxing Pass.
units.idiomatic: Next spring Jin attacked Tianchang Garrison. Rong sent relief, was beaten at Chiri Ridge, and Jin marched out through Jingxing Pass.

units.zh: 鎔又求救於匡威，晉軍解去。
units.literal: Rong again begged Kuangwei and Jin withdrew.
units.idiomatic: Rong begged Kuangwei again and Jin withdrew once more.

units.zh: 初，匡威悅其弟匡儔之婦美而淫之，匡儔怒，及其救镕也，誘其軍亂而自立。
units.literal: Earlier Kuangwei had coveted his brother Kuangchou’s wife for her beauty and lain with her; Kuangchou was enraged. When he came to rescue Rong he incited the army to mutiny and set himself up as ruler.
units.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei had taken his brother Kuangchou’s wife and seduced her; Kuangchou burned with anger. When he marched to save Rong he turned the troops against his brother and seized Youzhou for himself.

units.zh: 匡威內慚不敢還，乃以符印歸其弟，而將奔於京師。
units.literal: Ashamed within, Kuangwei dared not return; he returned the seals to his brother and prepared to flee to the capital.
units.idiomatic: Too ashamed to face his men, Kuangwei handed the seals to Kuangchou and set out for the capital.

units.zh: 行至深州，镕德匡威救己，使人邀之，館於梅子園，以父事之。
units.literal: When he reached Shenzhou, Rong, grateful that Kuangwei had saved him, sent men to invite him and lodged him at Meizi Garden, treating him as a father.
units.idiomatic: At Shenzhou, Rong—mindful that Kuangwei had saved him—sent for him and housed him at Meizi Garden, honoring him like a parent.

units.zh: 匡威客李正抱者，少遊燕、趙間，每徘徊常山，愛之不能去。
units.literal: Among Kuangwei’s followers was Li Zhengbao, who in youth had roamed Yan and Zhao and, lingering at Changshan, loved the place and could not leave.
units.idiomatic: One of Kuangwei’s companions was Li Zhengbao. As a young man he had wandered Yan and Zhao; each time he passed Changshan he lingered, unable to tear himself away.

units.zh: 正抱、匡威皆失國無聊，相與登城西高閣，顧覽山川，泫然而泣，乃與匡威謀劫而代之。
units.literal: Zhengbao and Kuangwei, both exiles with nothing to do, climbed the high pavilion west of the city, looked over the hills and rivers, wept, and plotted to seize Rong’s place.
units.idiomatic: Zhengbao and Kuangwei, both landless and idle, climbed the western tower, gazed over the landscape until they wept, and hatched a plan to seize Rong by force.

units.zh: 因詐為忌日，镕去衛從，晨詣館慰，坐定，甲士自幕後出，持镕兩袖，镕曰：「吾國賴公而存，誠無以報厚德，今日之事，是所甘心。」
units.literal: They feigned a day of mourning; Rong left his guards and came at dawn to the lodge to offer condolences. Once seated, armored men burst from behind the curtain and seized both his sleeves. Rong said: “Our state survived only through you—I have no way to repay such kindness. What you do today I accept willingly.”
units.idiomatic: They staged a memorial day. Rong came at dawn without escort to comfort Kuangwei at the lodge. As he sat down, soldiers in armor rushed from behind the screen and gripped his sleeves. Rong said: “You preserved our house—I could never repay you. Do as you will; I submit.”

units.zh: 因叩頭以位與匡威。
units.literal: He then kowtowed and yielded the throne to Kuangwei.
units.idiomatic: He kowtowed and offered Kuangwei the command.

units.zh: 匡威素少镕，以謂無能為也，因與镕方轡詣府，將代其位。
units.literal: Kuangwei had always looked down on the young Rong and thought him incapable; he rode side by side with Rong to the headquarters, about to take his place.
units.idiomatic: Kuangwei had always despised the boy and thought him harmless. He rode beside Rong to the yamen, ready to replace him.

units.zh: 行過親事營，軍士閉門大噪，天雨震電，暴風拔木，屋瓦皆飛。
units.literal: As they passed the personal-guard camp the soldiers shut the gates and raised a great clamor; rain fell, thunder rolled, a gale uprooted trees, and roof tiles flew through the air.
units.idiomatic: Passing the household guard camp, the troops slammed the gates and roared. Rain poured, lightning split the sky, wind tore up trees, and tiles flew from the roofs.

units.zh: 屠者墨君和望見镕，識之，從缺垣中躍出，挾镕於馬，負之而走，亂軍擊殺匡威、正抱，燕人皆走。
units.literal: The butcher Mo Junhe saw Rong, recognized him, leaped through a gap in the wall, seized him onto a horse, and carried him away; the mutineers killed Kuangwei and Zhengbao, and all the Yan men fled.
units.idiomatic: Mo Junhe the butcher spotted Rong, knew him, scrambled through a broken wall, hauled him onto a horse, and fled. The rebels killed Kuangwei and Zhengbao; every man from Yan ran.

units.zh: 匡儔雖憾其兄，而陽以大義責镕甚急。
units.literal: Though Kuangchou resented his brother, outwardly he pressed Rong hard with righteous blame.
units.idiomatic: Kuangchou hated his brother, yet in public he rebuked Rong in the name of justice.

units.zh: 镕既失燕援，而晉軍急攻平山，劫镕以盟，镕遂與晉和。
units.literal: Rong, having lost Yan’s support, faced Jin’s urgent assault on Pingshan; Jin took him hostage to force an alliance, and Rong made peace with Jin.
units.idiomatic: Cut off from Yan, Rong faced a fierce Jin attack on Pingshan. Jin held him to ransom for peace, and he submitted.

units.zh: 其後梁太祖下晉邢、洺、磁三州，乃為書詔镕，使絕晉而歸梁，镕依違不決。
units.literal: Later Liang Taizu took Jin’s Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures and sent an edict ordering Rong to break with Jin and return to Liang; Rong wavered, unable to decide.
units.idiomatic: When Liang Taizu seized Xing, Ming, and Ci from Jin he wrote Rong demanding he abandon Jin for Liang. Rong hesitated.

units.zh: 晉將李嗣昭復取洺州，梁太祖擊敗嗣昭，嗣昭棄洺州走。
units.literal: Jin’s general Li Sizhao retook Mingzhou; Liang Taizu defeated Sizhao, and Sizhao abandoned Mingzhou and fled.
units.idiomatic: Li Sizhao of Jin retook Mingzhou. Liang Taizu routed him, and Sizhao abandoned the city and fled.

units.zh: 梁獲其輜重，得镕與嗣昭書，多道梁事，太祖怒，因移兵常山，顧謂葛從周曰：「得鎮州以與爾，爾為我先鋒。」
units.literal: Liang captured the baggage train and found letters between Rong and Sizhao that spoke often of Liang’s affairs; the Taizu was furious, shifted his army to Changshan, and said to Ge Congzhou: “I give you Zhenzhou—be my vanguard.”
units.idiomatic: Liang took the supply train and found Rong’s letters to Sizhao, full of talk about Liang. Taizu flew into a rage, marched on Changshan, and told Ge Congzhou: “Zhenzhou is yours—lead the van.”

units.zh: 從周至臨城，中流矢，臥輿中，梁軍大沮。
units.literal: Congzhou reached Lincheng, took an arrow in the stream, and lay in a litter; the Liang army was greatly discouraged.
units.idiomatic: At Lincheng Congzhou took an arrow and had to be carried in a litter; Liang’s army lost heart.

units.zh: 梁太祖自將傅城下，焚其南關，镕懼，顧其屬曰：「事急矣！
units.literal: Liang Taizu personally led the assault below the walls and burned the south gate. Rong was afraid and said to his men: “Matters are desperate!
units.idiomatic: Taizu himself pressed the siege and fired the south gate. Rong, terrified, turned to his officers: “This is the end!

units.zh: 奈何？」
units.literal: What can we do?”
units.idiomatic: What can we do?"

units.zh: 式與梁太祖有舊，因請入梁軍。
units.literal: Shi had old ties with Liang Taizu and asked to enter the Liang camp.
units.idiomatic: Shi was an old acquaintance of Taizu’s and asked leave to go to the Liang lines.

units.zh: 太祖望見式，罵曰：「吾常以書招镕不來，今吾至此，而爾為說客，晚矣！
units.literal: Taizu saw him from afar and cursed: “I wrote again and again summoning Rong—he would not come. Now that I am here you play the envoy? Too late!
units.idiomatic: Taizu spotted him and raged: “I wrote Rong again and again—he ignored me. Now I am at his gates and you come as a go-between? It is too late!

units.zh: 且晉吾仇也，而镕附之，吾知李嗣昭在城中，可使先出。」
units.literal: And Jin is my enemy, yet Rong clings to them. I know Li Sizhao is in the city—have him come out first."
units.idiomatic: Jin is my enemy, and Rong sides with them. I know Sizhao is inside—send him out first."

units.zh: 乃以所得镕與嗣昭書示式，式進曰：「梁欲取一鎮州而止乎，而欲成霸業於天下也？
units.literal: He then showed Shi the captured letters. Shi advanced and said: “Does Liang mean to take only one Zhenzhou—or to win empire under Heaven?
units.idiomatic: He flung the letters before Shi. Shi stepped forward: “Does Liang want one prefecture—or the realm?

units.zh: 且霸者責人以義而不私，今天子在上，諸侯守封睦鄰，所以息爭，且休民也。
units.literal: A hegemon holds men to righteousness, not to private gain. Today the Son of Heaven sits above; the feudatories guard their fiefs and keep peace with their neighbors—that is how strife ends and the people rest.
units.idiomatic: A true conqueror judges by duty, not spite. The Son of Heaven still reigns; the circuits hold their borders and live as neighbors—that is how wars end and the people breathe.

units.zh: 太祖大喜，起牽式衣而撫之曰：「吾言戲耳。」
units.literal: The Taizu was greatly pleased, rose, took Shi by the robe, and stroked him, saying: “My words were in jest.”
units.idiomatic: Taizu laughed with delight, rose, took Shi by the sleeve, and said: “I was only testing you.”

units.zh: 因延式於上坐，議與镕和。
units.literal: He seated Shi in the place of honor and discussed peace with Rong.
units.idiomatic: He gave Shi the seat of honor and opened talks for peace with Rong.

units.zh: 镕以子昭祚為質，梁太祖以女妻之。
units.literal: Rong sent his son Zhaozuo as hostage; Liang Taizu gave him his daughter in marriage.
units.idiomatic: Rong sent his son Zhaozuo as hostage; Taizu married him to a Liang princess.

units.zh: 太祖即位，封镕趙王。
units.literal: When the Taizu took the throne he enfeoffed Rong Prince of Zhao.
units.idiomatic: When Taizu became emperor he made Rong Prince of Zhao.

units.zh: 镕祖母喪，諸鎮皆吊，梁使者見晉使在館，還言趙王有二誌。
units.literal: When Rong’s grandmother died every circuit sent condolences; a Liang envoy saw a Jin envoy in the lodge and reported that the Prince of Zhao had two minds.
units.idiomatic: At his grandmother’s funeral every circuit sent mourners. A Liang envoy saw Jin’s envoy at the same guesthouse and reported that the Zhao prince was playing both sides.

title.zh: 卷三百〇五 列傳第六十四 楊億 晁迥 劉筠 薛映
title.en: Volume 305 Biographies 64: Yang Yi, Chao Jiong, Liu Yun, Xue Ying
title.raw: 卷三百〇五 列傳第六十四 楊億 晁迥 劉筠 薛映 Volume 305 Biographies 64: Yang Yi, Chao Jiong, Liu Yun, Xue Ying

units.zh: 楊億，字大年，建州浦城人。
units.literal: Yang Yi, courtesy name Danian, was a native of Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.
units.idiomatic: Yang Yi, styled Danian, came from Pucheng in Jianzhou.

units.zh: 祖文逸，南唐玉山令。
units.literal: His grandfather Wenyi was magistrate of Yushan under the Southern Tang.
units.idiomatic: His grandfather Yang Wenyi had served as magistrate of Yushan under the Southern Tang.

units.zh: 億將生，文逸夢一道士，自稱懷玉山人來謁，未幾，億生，有毛被體，長尺餘，經月乃落。
units.literal: Before Yi was to be born, Wenyi dreamed that a Daoist who called himself the Hermit of Huaiyu came to pay a visit; before long Yi was born, his body covered with hair more than a foot long, which fell off only after a month.
units.idiomatic: Shortly before Yi's birth, Wenyi dreamed of a Daoist who introduced himself as the Hermit of Mount Huaiyu coming to call. Soon afterward Yi was born with hair covering his body, more than a foot in length, which did not fall away until a month had passed.

units.zh: 自邊境屢驚，凶黨猖熾，爵賞之而不恭，討罰之而無獲。
units.literal: Since the frontier has been repeatedly alarmed, the hostile bands have grown rampant; ennobled and rewarded, they show no deference; punished in campaigns, they are not taken.
units.idiomatic: Since the frontier has been repeatedly alarmed, the hostile bands have grown ever bolder. Honors and rewards win no deference from them, and punitive campaigns yield no captives.

units.zh: 自曹光實、白守榮、馬紹忠及王榮之敗，資糧屝屨，所失至多，將士丁夫，相枕而死。
units.literal: Since the defeats of Cao Guangshi, Bai Shourong, Ma Shaozhong, and Wang Rong, supplies and transport have been lost in great measure, and soldiers and corvée laborers have died piled upon one another.
units.idiomatic: Since the defeats suffered by Cao Guangshi, Bai Shourong, Ma Shaozhong, and Wang Rong, supplies and transport have been lost on a vast scale, and soldiers and corvée laborers have died in heaps upon the roads.

units.zh: 以至募商人輸帛入穀，償價數倍；
units.literal: Matters have reached the point of recruiting merchants to bring silk in exchange for grain, with reimbursement several times the cost;
units.idiomatic: Matters have reached the point where merchants are recruited to deliver grain in exchange for silk, with reimbursement several times the market price;

title.zh: 卷一百八十七 列傳第一百十二 二王諸葛李孟
title.en: Volume 187 Biographies 112: Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, Meng
title.raw: 卷一百八十七 列傳第一百十二 二王諸葛李孟 Volume 187 Biographies 112: Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, Meng

units.zh: 二王諸葛李孟
units.literal: The Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, and Meng
units.idiomatic: The Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, and Meng

units.zh: 王重榮，太原祁人。
units.literal: Wang Chongrong was a man of Qi in Taiyuan.
units.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 父縱，太和末為河中騎將，從石雄破回鶻，終鹽州刺史。
units.literal: His father Zong, at the end of the Taihe era served as a cavalry officer in Hezhong, followed Shi Xiong in defeating the Uyghurs, and ended as governor of Yanzhou.
units.idiomatic: His father Zong, in the closing years of the Taihe reign, served as a cavalry officer in Hezhong; he followed Shi Xiong against the Uyghurs and eventually became governor of Yanzhou.

units.zh: 克用以安金俊為邢州刺史，招撫之。
units.literal: Keyong appointed An Jinjun governor of Xing Prefecture to win the people over.
units.idiomatic: Keyong appointed An Jinjun governor of Xing Prefecture to pacify the region.

units.zh: 方立丐兵於王镕，镕以兵三萬赴之，克修還。
units.literal: Fangli begged troops from Wang Rong; Rong sent thirty thousand men to his aid, and Kexiu withdrew.
units.idiomatic: Fangli begged Wang Rong for troops; Rong sent thirty thousand men, and Kexiu withdrew.

units.zh: 後二年，方立督部將奚忠信兵三萬攻遼州，以金啖赫連鐸與連和。
units.literal: Two years later Fangli supervised his subordinate Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand troops to attack Liao Prefecture, bribing Helian Duo with gold to join in alliance.
units.idiomatic: Two years later Fangli led his subordinate Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand men against Liao Prefecture and bribed Helian Duo with gold to join him.

title.zh: 卷三十五 列傳第五 陳騫 裴秀
title.en: Volume 35 Biographies 5: Chen Qian; Pei Xiu
title.raw: 卷三十五 列傳第五 陳騫 裴秀 Volume 35 Biographies 5: Chen Qian; Pei Xiu

units.zh: 陳騫
units.literal: Chen Qian
units.idiomatic: Chen Qian

units.zh: 陳騫，臨淮東陽人也。
units.literal: Chen Qian was a man of Dongyang in Linhuai.
units.idiomatic: Chen Qian came from Dongyang in Linhuai commandery.

units.zh: 父矯，魏司徒。
units.literal: His father was Chen Jiao, Minister of Education of Wei.
units.idiomatic: His father, Chen Jiao, had served Wei as Minister of Education.

units.zh: 特為王綏所重，每從其遊。
units.literal: Wang Sui especially esteemed him and constantly accompanied him on outings.
units.idiomatic: Wang Sui especially esteemed him and constantly accompanied him on outings.

units.zh: 綏父戎謂之曰：「國寶初不來，汝數往，何也？」
units.literal: Sui's father Rong said to him: "Guobao never comes to you—why do you go to him so often?"
units.idiomatic: Sui's father Rong said to him: "Guobao never comes to you—why do you go to him so often?"

units.zh: 對曰：「國寶雖不知綏，綏自知國寶。」
units.literal: [Sui] replied: "Though Guobao does not know Sui, Sui knows Guobao."
units.idiomatic: He need not notice me," Sui said, "I notice him."

units.zh: 東海王越引為主簿，後為越子毗所害。
units.literal: Prince Donghai Yue took him as chief clerk; later Yue's son Pi murdered him.
units.idiomatic: Donghai heir Pi executed him.

units.zh: 初，裴、王二族盛于魏晉之世，時人以為八裴方八王：徽比王祥，楷比王衍，康比王綏，綽比王澄，瓚比王敦，遐比王導，頠比王戎，邈比王玄雲。
units.literal: At first the Pei and Wang houses flourished side by side in the Wei-Jin age; contemporaries likened eight Peis to eight Wangs: Hui to Wang Xiang, Kai to Wang Yan, Kang to Wang Sui, Chuo to Wang Cheng, Zan to Wang Dun, Xia to Wang Dao, Yi to Wang Rong, and Miao to Wang Xuan.
units.idiomatic: The Pei and Wang houses flourished in the Wei-Jin age; contemporaries likened eight Peis to eight Wangs: Hui to Wang Xiang, Kai to Wang Yan, Kang to Wang Sui, Chuo to Wang Cheng, Zan to Wang Dun, Xia to Wang Dao, Yi to Wang Rong, and Miao to Wang Xuan.

units.zh: 史評
units.literal: Historian's appraisal
units.idiomatic: Section heading for editorial judgement.

units.zh: 文苑四
units.literal: Literary Grove Four
units.idiomatic: Literary Grove, Part Four

units.zh: ○穆修石延年
units.literal: ○ Mu Xiu, Shi Yannian
units.idiomatic: Mu Xiu and Shi Yannian

units.zh: 〈（劉潛附）〉
units.literal: (Liu Qian appended)
units.idiomatic: (with Liu Qian appended)

units.zh: 及廣明之後，關東無復唐有，方鎮相侵伐者，猶以王室為名。
units.literal: After the Guangming era the east of the passes no longer belonged to Tang; when circuit commissioners invaded one another they still took the royal house as their name.
units.idiomatic: After the Guangming era the east of the passes no longer belonged to Tang; when circuit commissioners invaded one another they still took the royal house as their name.

units.zh: 及梁祖舉河南，劉仁恭輕戰而敗，羅氏內附，王鎔請盟，於時河北之事去矣。
units.literal: When the Liang founder raised Henan, Liu Rengong was defeated for fighting lightly, the Luo clan submitted within, and Wang Rong requested alliance—then Hebei affairs were gone.
units.idiomatic: When the Liang founder raised Henan, Liu Rengong was defeated for fighting lightly, the Luo clan submitted within, and Wang Rong requested alliance—then Hebei affairs were settled.

units.zh: 梁人一舉而代唐有國，諸侯莫能與之爭，其勢然也。
units.literal: The Liang in one move replaced Tang and held the realm; the feudatories could not contend with them—the trend was thus.
units.idiomatic: The Liang in one move replaced Tang and held the realm; the feudatories could not contend—the trend was thus.

title.zh: 卷三十三 列傳第十四 王僧虔 張緒
title.en: Volume 33 Biographies 14: Wang Sengqian, Zhang Xu
title.raw: 卷三十三 列傳第十四 王僧虔 張緒 Volume 33 Biographies 14: Wang Sengqian, Zhang Xu

units.zh: 南齊書卷三十三‧列傳第十四
units.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 33 — Biography 14
units.idiomatic: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 33 — Biography 14

units.zh: 王僧虔 張緒
units.literal: Wang Sengqian; Zhang Xu
units.idiomatic: Wang Sengqian; Zhang Xu

units.zh: 王僧虔，琅邪臨沂人也。
units.literal: Wang Sengqian was a native of Linyi in Langye.
units.idiomatic: Wang Sengqian was a man of Linyi in Langye.

units.zh: 第九子寂，字子玄，性迅動，好文章，讀《范滂傳》，未常不歎挹。
units.literal: His ninth son Ji, styled Zixuan, was quick and restless by nature, loved literature; reading the biography of Fan Pang, he never failed to sigh in admiration.
units.idiomatic: His ninth son Ji, styled Zixuan, was swift and restless by nature and loved letters; whenever he read the biography of Fan Pang he could not keep from sighing in wonder.

units.zh: 王融敗後，賔客多歸之。
units.literal: After Wang Rong's defeat, many clients turned to him.
units.idiomatic: After Wang Rong's fall, many of his former guests attached themselves to Ji.

units.zh: 建武初，欲獻《中興頌》，兄志謂之曰：「汝膏粱年少，何患不達，不鎮之以靜，將恐貽譏。」
units.literal: Early in Jianwu, he wished to present Ode on Restoration; his elder brother Zhi told him: "You are a young man of fattened grain—what need to worry you will not rise? If you do not steady yourself with quiet, you will probably invite ridicule."
units.idiomatic: At the opening of Jianwu he meant to offer an Ode on Restoration; his elder brother Zhi told him, "You are young, well-fed, and born to rank—what fear that you will not arrive? Without quiet to anchor you, you will only buy mockery."

units.zh: 山濤
units.literal: Shan Tao.

units.zh: 山濤，字巨源，河內懷人也。
units.en: Shan Tao, courtesy name Juyuan, came from Huai in Henei commandery.
units.literal: Shan Tao, courtesy name Juyuan, was a man of Huai in Henei.

source.zh: 山濤，字巨源，河內懷人也。

translations.literal: Shan Tao, courtesy name Juyuan, was a man of Huai in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao, courtesy name Juyuan, came from Huai in Henei commandery.

units.zh: 父曜，宛句令。
units.en: His father Shan Yao had been magistrate of Yuanju.
units.literal: His father Yao was magistrate of Yuanju.

translations.literal: His father Yao was magistrate of Yuanju.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shan Yao had been magistrate of Yuanju.

units.zh: 濤早孤，居貧，少有器量，介然不群。
units.en: Orphaned young and poor, he showed unusual breadth of character and stood apart from ordinary men.
units.literal: Tao early was orphaned, dwelt poor; in youth had capacity and tolerance—distinct not herd.

source.zh: 濤早孤，居貧，少有器量，介然不群。

translations.literal: Tao early was orphaned, dwelt poor; in youth had capacity and tolerance—distinct not herd.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, he showed unusual breadth of character and stood apart from ordinary men.

units.zh: 性好《莊》《老》，每隱身自晦。
units.en: He loved Zhuangzi and Laozi and kept deliberately out of the spotlight.
units.literal: By nature loved Zhuangzi and Laozi—often concealed body and dimmed himself.

translations.literal: By nature loved Zhuangzi and Laozi—often concealed body and dimmed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He loved Zhuangzi and Laozi and kept deliberately out of the spotlight.
